findings.title: Abort reported after the adapter wrote 101 but before onOpen is logged with status 200, not 101
findings.description: TinyHttpd writes the 101 in CapturingResponse.upgrade (TinyHttpdWebSocket.java:106-118, markUpgraded) before WebSocket.run calls listener.onOpen. An exchange abort in that window (e.g. TinyHttpdAdapter.stop aborting every exchange, TinyHttpdAdapter.java:195) makes DefaultResponse ABORTED while its status is still the default 200, so onOpen refuses and the single request line reads 'GET /ws 200 ... aborted' although the client received 101 on the wire. FR-APP-019 AC-3 says an after-commit abort logs 'its committed status'; whether the adapter-side 101 counts as the core response's commit is not specified. Not proven to break an AC; window is tiny and only reachable through adapter stop.
findings.suggested_fix: Either document that a refused open logs the pre-upgrade status, or have the refusal path record status 101 before the aborted line when the adapter reports the 101 as written.

findings.title: Error thrown from a ws handler aborts the NEW response of an open session with a second request line (pre-existing)
findings.description: opening() catches only Exception from h.handle; an Error escapes onOpen and ex.webSocket (upgrade catches IOException|RuntimeException only), reaching Dispatcher's catch (Error e) { res.abort(e); }. abort(e) is the non-exchange path, so sessionOpen does not gate it, and the still-NEW response writes 'GET /ws 200 ... aborted' after the '101' line.

findings.title: Refused session resource/registry handling
findings.description: Checked: a refused session never stores a channel, never sets opened, never acquires a sender slot or idle watch. onClose on it skips the close line and calls idle.unwatch / sender.release, both null-safe (WebSocketIdleScheduler:66-71, WebSocketSender:217-221); abort()/closeBy()/submit()/isOpen() are null-channel safe; sender.awaitIdle returns at once (WebSocketSender:152-156); registry.remove runs in WebSocketUpgrade.upgrade's finally, so no session-count leak; WebSocketRegistry.awaitDone waits for removal (bounded by the 1 s close wait), it does not block shutdown. res.upgraded() after a refusal is a no-op on ABORTED (DefaultResponse:939-943). TinyHttpd's WebSocket.run catches the IOException from the dropped connection and always delivers onClose (TinyHttpd WebSocket.java run/finally), so the refusal does not reach the error path with TinyHttpd. HttpExecution only calls public abort (byExchange=false) and never upgrades, so it is unaffected. No test weakened (test diff is additions only).
